title: Indian-Origin Teen in Massachusetts Charged With Killing Mother and Brother, Used ChatGPT to Script Family Killings
excerpt: Arjun Aravind, a high school student in Acton, Massachusetts, allegedly killed his mother Sudha Venkatesan and 14-year-old brother before fleeing in the family car.
body:
• Arjun Aravind, an Indian-origin teenager from Acton, Massachusetts, has been charged with two counts of murder in the deaths of his mother Sudha Venkatesan, 45, and younger brother Siddharth Aravind, 14.
  • Middlesex District Attorney Marian Ryan said the teen had been using ChatGPT to create fantasy stories and ask questions about how to kill his family members before the alleged killings on August 11.
  • The teen, a student at Acton-Boxboro Regional High School with interests in robotics and programming, was found by police in Wayland the morning after the killings in his mother's car.
  • Under Massachusetts law, anyone aged 14 or older charged with murder is treated as an adult.

An Indian-origin teenager in a quiet Boston suburb has been charged with murdering his mother and younger brother after authorities said he had been using ChatGPT to create graphic stories about killing his family in the weeks leading up to the attack.

Arjun Aravind is accused of killing his mother, Sudha Venkatesan, 45, and his brother, Siddharth Aravind, 14, at their home on Martha Lane in Acton, Massachusetts, on August 11. Middlesex District Attorney Marian Ryan announced the charges at a press conference at the Acton Police Department on Wednesday.

ChatGPT Fantasy Stories Preceded the Killings

In a detail that has drawn national attention to the case, Ryan revealed that the teenager had been using ChatGPT in the weeks before the alleged killings to create elaborate fantasy scenarios involving his family's deaths.

https://x.com/ABC/status/2087704764087759264

"He was engaged in the use of ChatGPT creating fantasy stories, kind of a graphic novel kind of story, asking questions, creating characters, asking questions about how to kill his family."

— Middlesex District Attorney Marian Ryan

Ryan said Aravind had recently been demonstrating concerning behaviour, including using the internet and the AI chatbot to search for "theoretical ideas or fantasy stories of the killing of his family." The district attorney did not specify whether the chatbot had provided actionable information or merely served as a platform for the teen's disturbing narratives.

Father's Call Led to Discovery

The investigation began at 6:37 p.m. on Tuesday when Aravind's father called police to conduct a welfare check. A visitor had been unable to enter the home, which was unusual. When the father could not reach family members by phone, he contacted authorities.

Officers who entered the Martha Lane residence found Venkatesan in a finished basement and Siddharth on the first floor. Both were suffering from what Ryan described as "obvious trauma." The cause and manner of death have not been determined; authorities are awaiting findings from the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner.

The father had last seen Venkatesan at 7 a.m. when he left for work. Siddharth had arrived home shortly after noon from a local recreational facility.

Captured After Overnight Flight

Investigators believe Aravind took his mother's car after the killings. Police issued an alert for the vehicle on Tuesday evening and searched the Shops at Highlands Commons area in Hudson and Berlin without success.

The break came Wednesday morning when Wayland Police responded to an unrelated alarm at a business on Andrew Avenue. Officers recognised a vehicle matching the description from the Acton alert and found Aravind inside. He was taken into custody without incident.

Aravind faces two counts each of murder, assault and battery with a dangerous weapon, and assault and battery on a family or household member. He is also charged with theft of a vehicle and using a vehicle without authority. He was expected to be arraigned on vehicle charges in Lowell Juvenile Court on August 12, with murder and assault charges to follow on August 13 in Concord District Court. Under Massachusetts law, anyone aged 14 or older who is charged with murder is tried as an adult.

A Student With No Prior Violent History

Aravind is a student at Acton-Boxborough Regional High School, a well-regarded public school in the western suburbs of Boston. According to his LinkedIn profile, he described himself as a "curious and motivated high school student" with interests in technology, business, finance, and marketing. He listed experience in programming languages including Java, C++, and Python, along with hands-on projects in robotics. He had advanced to the FIRST LEGO League World Championship.

Acton Police Chief Douglas Sturniolo said officers had dealt with Aravind once before when he had run away, but there were no prior reports of threatening behaviour.

A Community in Shock

Acton, a town of roughly 24,000 residents about 25 miles northwest of Boston, is home to a significant Indian-American community. The case has sent shockwaves through the tight-knit neighbourhood and the local school system.

"This is an unspeakable tragedy. It is an incredibly dark day. Obviously, an insurmountable tragedy for the dad in this case."

— Middlesex District Attorney Marian Ryan

The case has sent shockwaves through the community.dds to a growing body of incidents raising questions about the intersection of AI tools and violent ideation among young people. Several lawsuits against AI companies, including OpenAI, are currently making their way through US courts, alleging that chatbots have contributed to harmful behaviour in minors. This case marks one of the first instances where ChatGPT use has been cited as part of a homicide investigation involving a teenager.

Ryan said the investigation remains fluid and will continue as forensic and digital evidence is analysed.
